title: engineV3.1: checkpoints of the flowchart
source:
Source: `jfred/plans/puzzle-solver-rules.mmd`, live lines only (lines that do not start with `%%`), read 2026-11-21, from `B_LAUNCH` to `B_END_REGULAR_NODE_PROCESSING`. The `Q_INSIDE_REPO_AT_START` chain (old rules R3 to R16) and the script step are not in scope: they are not reachable from `B_LAUNCH` or they are a later feature.
This is not a build plan: no stages, no code design, no owners.

A stopping point is a node where the diagram says a result is now known or now built. A check proves that the code produces exactly that result. Every check fails when the result is wrong.
Existing functions are named with path:line from `plans/engineV3.1-existing-code-map.md` (called "the map" below). `engineV3/` and `src/` are under `jfred/`.
userDecisionsIntro: User decisions that the checks follow:

userDecisions.text: A file that is not on disk: the puzzle starts with the newest beacon found in the JSONLs or in git, not with an 'absent' node.

A full-file write without old text: skipped for now where no code handles it (map, Check 3: forward replay is handled, the before-state is not). First goal: a basic engine that is correct on commits and snapshots.
engineV3.1 uses its own new store, apart from the store of the current solver.
A file that moved: later (task 1092). Not in this list.
A range with script runs gets the status 'solved pending unreplayed script runs' and no 'user edit' node.

phases.name: find files
phases.userWords: The first chunk is finding all the files.

phases.name: find and place the events of each file
phases.userWords: The next chunk is finding all of the events for that particular file.

phases.name: split each puzzle into ranges
phases.userWords: The next chunk is splitting those events up into specific ranges based on beacons.

phases.name: replay the non-script events range by range
phases.userWords: The next chunk is then going through each of those ranges and trying to replay the non-script events.

phases.name: replay scripts
phases.userWords: Then the next chunk is to replay the script events for all of the files that a script touches.

checkpoints.text: Verify hash exists in git, Verify snapshots mentioned in JSONLs exist. Verify Project folder exists.

realCounts.measuredOn: 2026-11-21, read only. A Python script in the scratchpad read every JSONL of each folder once. The lookup rule is the one of findExistingBackupFile: a name is 'found' when <snapshot folder>/<JSONL file name without .jsonl>/<name> exists, or the same path under <snapshot folder>/file-history/. 'uniqueNamedBackups' counts each pair of session and name once.
realCounts.scenarioNote: The 20 scenarios have no file-history-delta records. Their snapshot folder is jfred/scenarios/file-history. The scenario JSONLs and snapshot folders are read only here.

existingFunctions: `getDefaultFileHistoryRoot` `src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts:15` and `findSiblingFileHistoryRoot` `:20`: the folder rule (plain code, no stop).

`getFileHistorySnapshot` `src/structures/file-history.ts:121`, type `FileHistoryBackup` `:6` (backupFileName is a string such as 463243de4cb9498e@v1 or null; version; backupTime; realParentDir), class `FileBackupMap` `:15`: how a snapshot record names its backup files (`snapshot.trackedFileBackups`, one entry per file path).

`listBackupsOfFile` `engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:436`: lists the backups of one file from one snapshot record. No function lists every name of a JSONL (code map `plans/engineV3.1-existing-code-map.md:36`, Gap B).

`findExistingBackupFile` `engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:458`: the lookup. For each snapshot folder it tries <folder>/<session id>/<name>, then <folder>/file-history/<session id>/<name>, and returns undefined when none exists.

`collectBackupKnownStates` `engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:472`: the caller. The session id is the JSONL file name without '.jsonl' (`:484`). It skips a null name and a missing file with no message (`:489`).

`findBackupOwner` `src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts:115`, `buildBackupPathResolver` `:128`, `buildSidecarReader` `:147`: the second rule in `src/`. It searches every session id of the records for the name, and the read at `:154` throws when the file is missing.
openQuestions: What does the run do with a missing snapshot? The diagram does not say. Today the engineV3 reader skips it with no message (`collectBackupKnownStates` `engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:489`), and the reader in `src/` throws when it reads the file (`src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts:154`). Not decided: stop with an error, record a research item, or skip.

Which session folder holds the copy? The engineV3 reader uses the JSONL file name as the session id (`engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:484`). The reader in `src/` searches every session id of the records (`findBackupOwner` `src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts:115`), because resumed or merged chats reuse names. Measured: 0 names are found only in another session's folder, in FX-INPUTS and in the 20 scenarios. Not decided which rule the new engine uses.

Do file-history-delta records count as snapshots named in the JSONL? FX-INPUTS has 211 of them (83 with a null backup, 128 unique names, all found). No code in `src/` or `engineV3/` reads them (only `src/structures/vocabulary.ts:20` lists the record type). The 20 scenarios have none. Not decided.
What makes two snapshot names 'the same'? Session id plus name, the name alone, or the path that was found. Today `collectBackupKnownStates` keeps a set of found paths (`seenBackupFiles`).

The recovery layout <folder>/file-history/<session id>/<name> is accepted by `findExistingBackupFile` (`engineV3/engineV3_replay_reverse.ts:455-466`) but not by `buildBackupPathResolver` (`src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts:142` builds only <root>/<session id>/<name>). Not decided which layouts the new engine accepts.
Is a file 'found' when it only exists, or when it can also be read as text and is not empty? Today the reader checks only that it exists (`existsSync`). Not decided.

Where does this stop sit? Point 6 needs the snapshot names as a source of file names, and the diagram has the node B_NEW_4 (`file-history snapshot path is pulled from JSONL file`) after B_DERIVE_SNAPSHOTS, in the singular. Whether this lookup goes before point 6 or inside it, and what the node id is, is not decided. The number 2 is kept.

checkpoints.text: verify that every event for this file could be replayed and consistently reproduce the same bytes in the Inverse-per-file-repo for this file.
expect a file tracked in git and deleted to show as deleted in git, and the previous
Every file in the found files list has at least 1 reconstruction event
a minimal git-only Inverse-Per-File-Repo can be created for this file.
a mentioned-in-JSONLs file F has at least 1 event in the events list.
the list of 'events for the file that need to be replayed' should exist and be non-empty.
the puzzle splits into ranges. every edit of the puzzle is in exactly one range. no edit is lost or doubled.
forward replay from the bytes of the older beacon, through every edit of the range, gives exactly the bytes that the newer beacon saw.
with the 'user edit' node in place, replay again from the older beacon reaches what the newer beacon saw. the range has no script runs.
with the 'user edit' node in place, replay again from the older beacon reaches what the newer beacon saw. the range has no script runs.
round trip. take the bytes that the backward replay ended with, replay the same edits forward, and get what the newer beacon saw again.
read the range back from the inverse per-file repo. the bytes of each node equal the bytes in memory. a second run answers 'already solved and saved: yes' for this range.
saved ranges + research ranges = all ranges of F. for a file on disk, the newest state in the inverse per-file repo equals the bytes on disk.
every included file finished its puzzle loop exactly once. the count of finished files equals the size of filesToReconstruct.
replay of the range from the script node to the newer beacon, with the bytes that the script made, gives exactly what the newer beacon saw.

diagramDoesNotSayIntro: Each item is a place where a check cannot be written clearly, or where decision a or b differs from the live text. These are not decided here.

diagramDoesNotSay.text: Decision a differs from the live text of `B_PUZZLE_START` (`Node 0 is the on-disk state of F (absent if F is not on disk)`), of `B_PUZZLE_ADD_GIT_COMMITS` (`a delete commit means absent`), of `B_RANGE_TAKE_FIRST` (`newer = puzzle[0];  (the on-disk state)`) and of `B_PUZZLE_REPLAY_START` (`The first range is 'now' and the first beacon after it.`). Under decision a, node 0 of a file that is not on disk is a beacon, not the on-disk state.

Decision a: events and commits that are newer than node 0 (node 0 is the newest beacon, not "now"). The nodes `Q_PUZZLE_EVENT_IN_PAIR` and `Q_PUZZLE_EVENT_BEFORE_OLDEST` place only events between nodes or older than the oldest. A JSONL Edit or a git commit newer than node 0 fits nowhere. Does it go to `B_RESEARCH_PUZZLE_EVENTS_FIT_NO_PAIR`, or is it dropped? Also what a git delete commit does when it is older or newer than node 0.

`B_BUILD_LIST_TO_RECONSTRUCT` (`Build the list of files to include or exclude for reconstruction`) comes before the per-file gate (`B_FILE_NAMED_IN_LOGS` then `Q_NEW_6`). The node text says the list has includes and excludes, but the marks are made later per file. `B_NEW_9` and `B_NEW_10` have the same text and the diagram does not say what `B_NEW_9` (exclude) and `B_NEW_10` (include) hand to the next step.

`B_SOURCE_DISK`, `B_SOURCE_GIT`, `B_SOURCE_SUBMODULE_GIT`, `B_SOURCE_LOGS`, `B_FIND_GIT_FOLDER_OF_F` and `B_NEW_12` appear only in `class` lines. They have no text and no edge. The four sources are described only by the notes above `B_ALL_INPUTS_KNOWN`.

`B_NEW_4` (`file-history snapshot path is pulled from JSONL file`) follows `B_DERIVE_SNAPSHOTS` (`Derive the snapshot folder path from the project folder`). The two texts name different ways to find the snapshot folder. It also says "path" (one) where the given case says "folders" (several).
How `B_DERIVE_JSONLS`, `B_DERIVE_SNAPSHOTS`, `B_DERIVE_GIT_FOLDER` derive: the diagram says "derive" only. The checks above use the existing default rules (map block 1).

`Q_REMOVED_FROM_REPO_IN_GIT` and `Q_NEW_1` (`in F's git folder`, `latest event in F's git folder`): which git folder, for a file in a submodule or outside the project; and `Q_NEW_1` does not say whether "latest" is up to the chosen hash or up to HEAD. `Q_NEW_2` (`Was the removal event before or after the commit time of the git hash?`) does not say what an equal time does.

`B_PUZZLE_LIST_EVENTS` says "every event ... that modifies F", but `B_PUZZLE_PICK_BEST_EVENT` ranks `commit, snapshot, full-file read, full-file write, then partial edit`. A snapshot and a full-file read do not modify F; a commit is not a JSONL event (commits come from `B_PUZZLE_ADD_GIT_COMMITS`). The diagram does not say which of these go into `events`. It also does not rank "Edit with originalFile" (a beacon in `B_PUZZLE_REPLAY_START`, but not named in the pick list).

Event kinds not named anywhere in the live flow: partial Read, `UserEditNotice`, `OtherRow` (open question 3 of the build plan). Where they go in `events`, and whether they count as edits inside a range, is not said.

`Q_PUZZLE_EVENT_IN_PAIR` (`Does any listed event lie between the two nodes of this pair?`): strictly between is implied by `B_RESEARCH_PUZZLE_EVENTS_FIT_NO_PAIR` (same time as a node) but not written. Events without an instant are not mentioned. (A measurement on 2705 real records found no equal-instant pair; map, Check 2. Git commit times have second precision and were not measured.)

`B_RANGE_START_BYTES` (`bytes = older.bytes`): for an older beacon that is an Edit with originalFile or a full-file write, "its bytes" could mean the text after the event or its originalFile. `Q_RANGE_BYTES_EQUAL_NEWER` says "what the newer beacon saw" (originalFile) for the newer side only.

Decision b differs from the live text of: `B_PUZZLE_PICK_BEST_EVENT` (full-file write is ranked), `B_PUZZLE_REPLAY_START` (full-file write is a beacon), `Q_RANGE_BYTES_EQUAL_NEWER` and `Q_CHOICE_RANGE_BYTES_EQUAL_NEWER_CANNOT_TELL` (`Cannot tell: full-file write without originalFile` goes to status `solved` or `pending` without a compare), `B_RANGE_BACKWARD_START` (`or its originalFile`). The map (Check 3) shows: existing code handles a full-file write without old text as a forward beacon but not as a before-state; skipping the event removes a full reset of the bytes. Not decided: skip as a newer beacon only, or drop the event.

`B_RANGE_INSERT_USER_EDIT_BEFORE_NEWER` (`Insert a 'user edit' node before the newer beacon. It gets what the newer beacon saw`): "before" in list order or in time is not said; which bytes the node holds before it (the replay result) is not said; whether the node splits the saved range into two ranges is not said. The check in 26 follows the reading "just older than the newer beacon, after-bytes equal to what the newer beacon saw".

`Q_RANGE_ANY_EDIT_LEFT` (`Is there an edit left to replay/reverse (depending on which engine gets used) between older and newer?`): "which engine gets used" is not defined; the backward loop has its own question `Q_RANGE_ANY_EDIT_LEFT_BACKWARD`. `Q_RANGE_ANY_EDIT_LEFT_BACKWARD` says `after a 'user edit' node: stop after the edit that did not apply`, but the forward loop does not say how the failing edit is remembered for the backward loop.

`B_RANGE_UNDO_EDIT` (`The next node further in history gets bytes`) and `B_RANGE_SAVE` (`Write the range and its range status`): what is written for each node (all nodes, or only beacons and the 'user edit' nodes) and in which format is not said. The checks in 29 use read-back of the range, the edits and the status only.
A git delete commit as the older beacon of a range (`B_RANGE_START_BYTES`): `bytes` absent is not defined for the replay (an edit on absent bytes).

`Q_RANGE_SOLVED_SAVED` (`same bytes of older, same bytes of newer, same events between them`): the key of the saved range is not defined (hash of the bytes? the ids of the events?). With a new store (decision c) the first run has nothing saved, so the Yes branch can be checked only on a second run.

`B_PUZZLE_BARRIER` (`the puzzle loop of every included file is finished`): a file that ended at `B_RESEARCH_PUZZLE_EVENTS_FIT_NO_PAIR` flows to `Q_PUZZLE_MORE_FILES` and counts as finished. What is saved for that file is not said.

`B_HISTORY_COMPLETE_IN_GIT` (`The change history for this file is complete, and the puzzle for this file is considered solved`) is followed by `Q_NEW_2`, so a "solved" file can still be included (after the hash). Whether a solved file is marked in the store when it is included is not said.

The order of files inside one group (`B_PROCESS_GROUPS_IN_ORDER`, `B_PUZZLE_NEXT_FILE`: `Take the next file in the current group. advance the group number if the group is finished.`) is not defined; the check in 12 asserts only the non-decreasing group numbers.

scenariosIntro: Expected result of each stopping point on the 20 recorded scenarios listed in "How each stopping point is verified". One sub-section per scenario. Each row: stopping point number, expected value, mark. Marks: "worked out from the scenario files", "guess", or "blocked by item N" (item N of "Diagram does not say"). Node names (W1, E1, S1 and so on) are local to the sub-section. `P` is the recorded folder `jfred/scenarios/executed/<scenario>`. A scenario folder with several runs uses its newest run.

scenarios.name: s13-multi-edit-code-restore-read
scenarios.facts:

scenarios.name: s1-delete-file
